topic: Side slip sensing and turn co-ordination, location of sensing elements in the A/C and explanation of inertial attitude references.
syllabus_extract: Side slip sensing and turn co-ordination, location of sensing elements in the A/C and explanation of inertial attitude references.
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of AFCS sensing element locations on aircraft diagrams; Instructor supervision during diagram analysis.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the AFCS?
Where are the side slip sensing elements typically located?

development.content:
Side slip sensing mechanism
Turn co-ordination principles
Sensing element locations in A/C
Inertial attitude reference explanation

AFCS operational logic
Error detection via inertial refs
Turn coordination feedback loops

Integration of side slip data
Inertial reference stability
AFCS output generation

summary_questions: Explain how side slip sensing contributes to turn coordination.
Describe the role of inertial attitude references in AFCS function.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the concepts of side slip sensing and inertial attitude references discussed in this lesson will be utilized in the study of inductive elements like EI bar and Synchro in the next lesson plan.

pft_rows.syllabus: Inductive element like EI bar and Synchro as an error detection element in FCS, torque synchro, control synchro, differential and Resolver synchro.
